title: Circuit size after hardwiring inputs
statement: Let $a,p : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$, and for each $n$ let $D_n$ be a Boolean circuit on $n+a(n)$ input bits and let $\alpha_n$ be a fixed Boolean string of length $a(n)$. Suppose every $D_n$ is well formed with fan-in at most two, and its size is at most $p(n)$. Then the language consisting of Boolean strings $w$ for which $D_{|w|}$ accepts the concatenation of $w$ and $\alpha_{|w|}$ is recognized by a family of fan-in-two Boolean circuits of size at most $p(n)$ on inputs of length $n$.
